title.value: DiPS: Discriminative Pseudo-Label Sampling with Self-Supervised Transformers for Weakly Supervised Object Localization
title.justification: The title reflects the core contribution of the paper, which is the introduction of the Discriminative Pseudo-Label Sampling (DiPS) method for improving weakly supervised object localization using self-supervised transformers.
title.quote: In this paper, Discriminative Pseudo-label Sampling (DiPS) is introduced to leverage these class-agnostic maps for weakly-supervised object localization (WSOL), where only image-class labels are available.

analysis.description: This paper introduces DiPS, a method that leverages self-supervised vision transformers to improve weakly supervised object localization by generating discriminative pseudo-labels. The approach aims to optimize both classification and localization tasks using class-agnostic attention maps from SSTs, which are processed using a pre-trained classifier to identify discriminative regions. These identified regions are used as pseudo-labels for training a new transformer-based model.

type.justification: The paper focuses on the empirical evaluation of DiPS, comparing it against state-of-the-art methods on several datasets, highlighting improved performance in weakly supervised object localization tasks.
type.quote: Experimental results on the challenging CUB, ILSVRC, OpenImages, and TelDrone datasets indicate that our architecture, in combination with our transformer-based proposals, can yield better localization performance than state-of-the-art methods.
